subject.title: memory-wiki vault-page reads have zero agent/session scoping, letting a sandboxed sub-agent read another agent's bridged memory content

question: Should this public memory-wiki cross-agent content-disclosure report be handled through the security/advisory path before any automated fix work is staged?
rationale: The source-backed bug crosses an agent/sandbox data boundary, and repository policy routes security-sensitive work away from ordinary automated repair unless maintainers explicitly choose the handling path.

options.title: Route Through Security Review
options.body: Keep the public issue open but have a maintainer/security owner decide disclosure, patch ownership, and release handling before repair work starts.

options.title: Proceed As Public Bug
options.body: Treat the report as already-public hardening and let maintainers sponsor a normal fix PR with focused regression proof.

options.title: Consolidate With Sibling
options.body: Use this issue as the content-disclosure canonical item and link the weaker status/count leak as same-root follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Route Through Security Review
recommendation.body: Keep the public issue open but have a maintainer/security owner decide disclosure, patch ownership, and release handling before repair work starts.

likelyOwner.reason: The central bridge and wiki-corpus surfaces trace most directly to vincentkoc's feature-history commits.
